The proof chose an optimal initial plan without citing the attainment supplier. A finite-action continuity-equation solution has its defined repository meaning from def-continuity-equation-with-finite-action: the opening clause requires a narrowly continuous curve in P2(Rd). Thus the proposed constant infinite-second-moment counterexample is inadmissible. The superposition supplier inherits that definition, so Z0 belongs to path-space L2; finite action propagates the norm bound, and disintegrating at t proves the derivative inequality for every optimal plan.

F4 incorrectly attributed a measurable minimum section to AC/Bochner suppliers. It now assigns only inherited countable-choice approximation duties to them and explicitly assigns selection measurability and the norm bound to F2. On coupling labels the semiconvex Hilbert inequality gives the asserted all-coupling inequality; conversely deterministic perturbations recover the Hilbert supporting inequality, proving minimum-norm uniqueness.

The cited F2 supplier lem-localized-lift-subdifferential proves, in steps 1.2 and 4.1, coercive resolvent existence, its Lipschitz estimate, the (1+epsilon alpha)|z_epsilon|^2 projection bound, and convergence to the full shifted minimum. These are precisely the argument explicitly invoked in step 2.3; the envelope C1 formula is proved there by two comparisons. The L2 gradient-closure approximation and orthogonality to every competing velocity then establish minimum action. No missing mathematical premise was found.

The cited lift lemma explicitly proves dot X(t,s)=v_t(X(t,s)) for almost every (t,s) in proof step 1.1, by the minimum-norm Hilbert-flow theorem and exact lifted minimum-section formula. That step also proves equality of Hilbert and Eulerian actions. The theorem uses precisely that identity in step 2.1. The EVI combines the distance derivative with the all-coupling subgradient inequality with the correct sign; characteristic stability gives uniqueness and contraction. No item edit is needed.

The second stability quantifier did not state the P2 domain required to define W2 and the flows; cutoff sets can be unbounded, so concentration alone is insufficient. Added mu0,nu0 in P2(Omega), preserving the intended flow domain and estimate. The patching proof and global competitor uniqueness use the escape bound and continuous-forcing characteristics. Also chose KT nonnegative before taking the time supremum.

The localized lift equals Fm only when every particle is in the chosen cutoff. Corrected F1 and step 1.1 to state Er=Fm on Qr^m and Er=+infinity outside. The two-sided chain-rule argument yields finite action, Hilbert uniqueness identifies the atomic flow, and a common escape radius gives the claimed deterministic W2 estimate.
